simple: Properties are the built-in settings of an object, like a part's `Size` or `Color`. Attributes are your own custom settings you add, like `Price = 50` or `Harvestable = true`. This page shows how to find objects, change their properties, add and read attributes, and run code when any of them change. It also explains why client scripts should use `WaitForChild`, because things load in an unknown order.
analogy: Properties are like the facts printed on a trading card (name, color, size). Attributes are like sticky notes you add yourself, such as 'worth 50 coins' or 'can be harvested'.
keyPoints: Get an object with `script.Parent` if the script is inside it, or with `FindFirstChild` and `WaitForChild` from a service.
Change a property with a dot: `part.Size = Vector3.new(10, 1, 10)`.
`SetAttribute("Name", value)` creates or changes an attribute. Set it to `nil` to delete it.
`GetAttribute("Name")` reads one attribute; `GetAttributes()` gives a table of all of them.
Listen for changes with `Changed` (any property), `AttributeChanged` (any attribute), `GetPropertyChangedSignal("Name")` (one property), or `GetAttributeChangedSignal("Name")` (one attribute).
Roblox does not promise the order things are copied from the server to players, so client scripts should use `WaitForChild` instead of assuming something exists.
On joining, the client loads ReplicatedFirst first, then the rest of the game, then runs PlayerScripts, then spawns the character and runs character scripts.
Changes of the same type, like two attribute changes, usually arrive in order.

terms.property: A built-in setting on an object, like a part's `Size`, `Color`, or `Anchored`.
terms.attribute: A custom setting you add to an object yourself, like `GrowthRate = 2`.
terms.replication: Copying objects and changes from the server to each player's device.
terms.replication order: The order things arrive on a player's device. It is not guaranteed, so something might not be there yet when your script runs.
terms.reference: A variable that points to an object so you can work with it, like `local sign = script.Parent`.
terms.WaitForChild: Waits until a child with that name exists, then gives it to you. Safe for client scripts.
terms.FindFirstChild: Looks for a child with that name right now. Returns `nil` if it is not there yet.
terms.signal: Another word for an event you can connect a function to.
terms.anonymous function: A function with no name, written right inside `:Connect(function() ... end)`.
terms.dictionary: A table with named keys, like `{ GrowthRate = 2, Harvestable = true }`.

example.title: A crop that becomes harvestable
example.place: Script inside a Part named Cabbage in Workspace
example.code:
local cabbage = script.Parent

-- Create attributes with starting values
cabbage:SetAttribute("Harvestable", false)
cabbage:SetAttribute("GrowthRate", 2)

-- Run code whenever Harvestable changes
cabbage:GetAttributeChangedSignal("Harvestable"):Connect(function()
	if cabbage:GetAttribute("Harvestable") then
		cabbage.Color = Color3.fromRGB(0, 200, 0) -- turn bright green
		print("The cabbage is ready!")
	end
end)

-- Wait a few seconds, then make it harvestable
task.wait(10 / cabbage:GetAttribute("GrowthRate")) -- 5 seconds
cabbage:SetAttribute("Harvestable", true)
explain: We add two attributes to the cabbage: `Harvestable` and `GrowthRate`.
We listen for changes to just `Harvestable` with `GetAttributeChangedSignal`.
When it becomes true, we change the cabbage's `Color` property to green.
We wait 10 divided by the growth rate (10 / 2 = 5 seconds), then set `Harvestable` to true, which fires our listener.

watchOut: Attribute names are case-sensitive. `GetAttribute("growthrate")` will not find `GrowthRate`.
In client scripts, use `WaitForChild` for objects from the server. Using a dot right away can error if the object has not arrived yet.
`GetPropertyChangedSignal` and `GetAttributeChangedSignal` do not tell you the new value. Read it inside your function.
A Model does not have properties like `Size` or `Color` the way parts do. Pick the part inside the model to change those.
